subject: 2 Questions: Subset of questions continuous responses and invariance specifications with n>2 groups

messages.author: 28107d5fea397fff
messages.subject: 2 Questions: Subset of questions continuous responses and invariance specifications with n>2 groups
parts:
Hi Phil, 

I have two questions related to the best way to use mirt and IRT for my use case. I have a larger number of groups (n > 10) which all use different test forms with some overlapping questions.  The questions have a combination of binary, categorical and continuous response options. I want to use the multipleGroup() function for test equating. 

My first question relates to how to deal with the questions that have continuous (or functionally continuous) responses (example: scale of 0-32).  Is it correct that mirt cannot deal with continuous responses? Are there other methods available potentially included in other software that could handle continuous responses? To solve this, I am currently dividing any item with more than 10 response options into quartiles and treating the question as ordinal categorical. For items with 10 responses or less I am specifying ordinal categorical without changing the scale. Is the 10 item response cutoff reasonable? Can you think of a better way of dealing with this without losing information from cutting the responses in quartiles?

My second question relates to the specification of anchor items and parameter invariance across a larger number of groups. An example of the structure of groups and questions is shown in the image attached. Sets of questions are wide and groups of individuals are long. Filled in blocks are where a group answered that group of questions, NA blocks are questions that did not get asked to a specific group. I understand that for the two group case, for questions that were asked to one group and not the other, I would want to specify the column names in the invariance argument, so that only one set of parameters would be estimated. However, how would you handle the three group case, where I want different parameters estimated for two of the groups (because there is evidence that the question functions differently between those two groups) but for the third group I don't really want any parameters estimated because the group was not administered those questions. Additionally, there could be a case in which all three groups are administered the same question and for two of the groups the parameters should be estimated as the same, but for the third group there is DIF and different parameters should be estimated. Ideally, instead of specifying invariance as column names, it would make sense if the specification could be a matrix that would tell you where parameter values could differ across groups and questions. Can you think of a way that I could handle this type of structure in mirt? If not possible in mirt, do you know of other software that would be able to handle this? 

Thanks so much, 
Emma

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: 2 Questions: Subset of questions continuous responses and invariance specifications with n>2 groups
parts:
Hi Emma,

Sorry it took me so long to reply to your email. I recently made a rather abrupt international move back to Canada, so much of my life was put on hold for nearly two months. Fortunately, it's finally starting to smooth out again. 

Regarding your questions. Currently, mirt cannot deal with continuous response formats. That's not to say it couldn't, as theoretically this is possible. I agree without your current approach though to truncating the continuous measure into something with fewer parameters, particularly if you have a smaller sample size. Regarding the 10 size recommendation, that has more to do with your sample size and frequency of the collapsed categories than anything else (you don't want the binned categories to be too small, otherwise intercept parameter estimates can be very large and unstable).

My second question relates to the specification of anchor items and parameter invariance across a larger number of groups. An example of the structure of groups and questions is shown in the image attached. Sets of questions are wide and groups of individuals are long. Filled in blocks are where a group answered that group of questions, NA blocks are questions that did not get asked to a specific group. I understand that for the two group case, for questions that were asked to one group and not the other, I would want to specify the column names in the invariance argument, so that only one set of parameters would be estimated. However, how would you handle the three group case, where I want different parameters estimated for two of the groups (because there is evidence that the question functions differently between those two groups) but for the third group I don't really want any parameters estimated because the group was not administered those questions.

You can set the third groups parameters to be equal to either the first or second groups; it makes no difference in the estimation because the third group does not contribute to the likelihood equations. For this setup, you may find it easier to work with the complete syntax form documented in ?mirt.model, which should help you with the parameter equivalence specification (see the [ ] notation to explicitly select groups).

Additionally, there could be a case in which all three groups are administered the same question and for two of the groups the parameters should be estimated as the same, but for the third group there is DIF and different parameters should be estimated. Ideally, instead of specifying invariance as column names, it would make sense if the specification could be a matrix that would tell you where parameter values could differ across groups and questions. Can you think of a way that I could handle this type of structure in mirt? If not possible in mirt, do you know of other software that would be able to handle this?

Yes, see the mirt.model() syntax for this as well. Cheers.

Phil
 

Thanks so much, 
Emma
